text:
Jordan Park: Hi team, new hire here. Trying to run the local compose stack on my MacBook Air (M1) — postgres + redis + web. Postgres container is up but my local dev server (running on host) can't connect: connection refused on localhost:5432. I noticed postgres service in compose doesn't publish a port (we rely on the compose network). Should I change that or is there a better pattern? Also Redis asks for a password in production but I don't want to commit creds in the repo. Any tips?

Leah Martinez: Welcome Jordan! For Mac, if your app runs on the host (not in docker), use host.docker.internal:5432 to reach a container port. If compose doesn't publish a port you can add: 
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
```
But keep in mind that exposing ports is less isolated. Another pattern is run the app inside the same compose as a service so it can hit the service name (postgres).

Carlos Vega: Re: redis creds, we keep a dev-only env file (.env.local) that's gitignored with REDIS_PASSWORD=devpass. The compose file uses env interpolation: `REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}` and we mount a small redis.conf in dev that disables requirepass. If you don't want to create files, you can override the command for dev: `command: redis-server --requirepass ""` or set `REDIS_PASSWORD=` in .env.local.

Jordan Park: Ah ok that explains the host.docker.internal bit. I tried adding ports: - "5432:5432" but docker-compose says port is already in use. I do have a local postgres installed via homebrew. How do people avoid conflicts?

Leah Martinez: Either stop the host postgres (brew services stop postgresql) or change the mapped host port, e.g. "15432:5432" and point your app to host.docker.internal:15432. We usually pick 15xxx for local overrides.

Carlos Vega: One more gotcha on M1: some postgres images default to linux/amd64. If you see errors like "exec format error" the image isn't arm64. Use `image: postgres:15-alpine` or add `platform: linux/amd64` (slower, uses emulation). We prefer arm64-compatible images when possible.

Jordan Park: Good call, I saw `exec format error` earlier and switched tags. After stopping brew postgres and exposing 15432 it connects, but my app complains that the DB user doesn't exist. I have an init SQL in ./db/init/ create-user.sql mounted to /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d but it didn't run — logs say "database directory appears to contain a database; skipping initialization"

Leah Martinez: That means the data dir already had files. If you're mapping a host dir to /var/lib/postgresql/data, the entrypoint only runs init on an empty dir. To reset: `docker-compose down -v` then remove the host dir contents `rm -rf ./pgdata/*` (if using a host bind) or remove the named volume with `docker volume rm <compose_project>_pgdata`. After that, `docker-compose up` will re-run the init scripts.

Jordan Park: I used a named volume in compose but didn't know the volume name. How do I find & remove it?

Carlos Vega: `docker volume ls` to list, then `docker volume inspect <name>` to check mountpoint. For compose v2 project name is usually the folder name. If you want to remove all unused volumes `docker volume prune` (careful).

Jordan Park: Quick question about mounting init scripts: my local editor (VSCode) sets files to 0640 by default. Could permission bits prevent the entrypoint from reading them?

Leah Martinez: Yes, the entrypoint runs as the postgres user inside container. Make sure files are world-readable or chown them: `chmod 644 ./db/init/*.sql`. You can also bind as read-only with :ro but still needs to be readable.

devops-bot: Reminder: internal dev guide at https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-setup has recommended compose snippets for Mac M1, port mappings, and a sample .env.local.template.

Carlos Vega: If you want to avoid changing host ports, another pattern: run the dev web server in docker-compose too and add a small override `docker-compose.override.yml` for dev only that includes the app service. That keeps everything in the same network and avoids host<->container networking issues.

Jordan Park: Thanks all 97 that unblocked me. I'll stop my brew postgres, chmod the init scripts, remove the named volume and bring up compose again. If I hit anything else I'll ping in here or DM. Appreciate the help!
